messages.author: 3ef7a01c7d912ca2
messages.subject: print trims
parts:
When using rstan 1.3 in RStudio, Windows 7, R 3.0.1, the print statement seems to trim whitspace from each partial statement, so to get readable output I have to use some other delimiter than space:

print("n= ",n,"  -  -Minute= ",Minute[n]);
               ^^ < Note that the trailing spaces are removed

n= 10-  -Minute= 137


Dieter Menne

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] print trims
parts:
On 5/24/13 4:49 AM, Dieter Menne wrote:
> When using rstan 1.3 in RStudio, Windows 7, R 3.0.1, the print statement seems to trim whitspace from each partial
> statement, so to get readable output I have to use some other delimiter than space:
>
> print("n= ",n," - -Minute= ",Minute[n]);
> ^^ < Note that the trailing spaces are removed
>
>
> n= 10- -Minute= 137

That's not something in our RStan code, is it?

I wonder what RStudio did, because the print statement
you provided doesn't work in the regular R GUI.

> print("n= ",10," y=",12)
Error in print.default("n= ", 10, " y=", 12) : invalid 'quote' argument

And if I do this, I only get the first one.

> print("n=",10)
[1] "n="

Check out the help for print --- the first argument gets
printed (which function gets used is determined by R's
OO system, which I don't understand), and the rest is config.

I can use this:

> print(c("n= ",10," y= ",12),quote=F)
[1] n= 10 y= 12

or you can get fancier and control with paste:

> print(paste("n= ",10,"; y= ",100, sep=""),quote=F)
[1] n= 10; y= 100

There's also sprintf() if you want more formatting.

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] print trims
parts:
I figured out he meant the print in Stan.  This is a detailed example. 

> code <- '
+ transformed data {
+   real a;
+   a <- 3;
+   print("a=", " [", a, "]");
+ }
+ parameters {
+   real y;
+ }
+ 
+ model {
+   y ~ normal(0, 1);
+ } 
+ '
> 
> stan(model_code = code, chains = 1, iter = 2)

TRANSLATING MODEL 'a' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'a' NOW.
a=[3]
SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'a' NOW (CHAIN 1).
Iteration: 2 / 2 [100%]  (Sampling)
Elapsed Time: 0 seconds (Warm Up)
              0 seconds (Sampling)
              0 seconds (Total)

> 

--
Jiqiang
